prompt: Why does `postgres:17` have no slash in its name, while most images on Docker Hub look like `someone/something`?
hint: The pull printed the full name.

choices.text: Slashes are not allowed in database image names
choices.why: Any image may have a namespace; this one's is hidden by default.

choices.text: It is stored on Ana's machine, not on Docker Hub
choices.why: It was pulled from Docker Hub, through the mirror.

choices.text: PostgreSQL owns the domain `docker.io`
choices.why: The registry is Docker's; `library` is its namespace for official images.

choices.text: An official image, in the `library` namespace
choices.why: Right: `docker` fills the namespace in, `docker.io/library/postgres:17`.

prompt: `postgres:17` has `Entrypoint` `docker-entrypoint.sh` and `Cmd` `postgres`. What runs when Ana starts it with no command?

choices.text: The script, with `postgres` passed as its argument
choices.why: Right. The script prepares things and then starts the server.

choices.text: `postgres` alone; the entrypoint only runs on first start
choices.why: The entrypoint always runs, and decides what to do on first start.

choices.text: A shell, because no command was given
choices.why: That is alpine's default `Cmd`; this image has its own.

choices.text: Both programs at once, in two processes
choices.why: The command is an argument to the entrypoint, not a second process.

prompt: The image declares `ExposedPorts` `5432/tcp`. Without any `-p`, can a program on Ana's host connect to the database on `localhost:5432`?

choices.text: Yes, Docker publishes declared ports
choices.why: Declaring a port documents it; nothing is published until `-p` asks.

choices.text: No
choices.why: Right. `ExposedPorts` is documentation; lesson 17 publishes ports.

choices.text: Only programs running as root
choices.why: It is not about privileges; nothing is listening on the host at all.

choices.text: Yes, but only for a minute after the container starts
choices.why: There is no window; without `-p` there is no published port.

prompt: Match each `postgres` tag to what it names.
hint: Some move more often than others.

pairs.right: The newest 17.x release, moving with every patch
The same PostgreSQL built on Alpine

right_distractors: A build that never changes, guaranteed by Docker

prompt: `docker exec db pg_isready` said ready, then `psql -h 127.0.0.1` from the host failed with "server closed the connection unexpectedly". What was `pg_isready` actually talking to?
hint: Where did it look, and which server was running then?

choices.text: The real server, which then crashed
choices.why: Nothing crashed; the log shows an orderly handover.

choices.text: The PostgreSQL on Ana's host
choices.why: It ran inside the container, through `docker exec`.

choices.text: The temporary setup server, on the Unix socket
choices.why: Right. It listens only on the socket, so the check passed and TCP clients could not connect.

choices.text: Nothing; `pg_isready` always says ready
choices.why: It said not ready until the temporary server came up.

prompt: Which check waited until the database really accepted outside connections?
hint: Ask the way the clients will connect.

choices.text: `docker ps` showing the container as `Up`
choices.why: `Up` means the main process runs, which it did all along.

choices.text: `pg_isready` with no host inside the container
choices.why: That is the one that answered for the temporary server.

choices.text: Waiting until `docker logs` prints anything at all
choices.why: The temporary server prints plenty before the real one starts.

choices.text: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1` inside the container
choices.why: Right: over TCP, which the temporary server does not listen on.

prompt: Put the image's first start in order.
items: The entrypoint creates the data files
A temporary server starts, on the Unix socket only
The real server starts and listens on TCP 5432

prompt: Ana restarted the database against the same volume with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=other`, and that password was refused. What would make `other` work?
hint: When does the image read that variable?

choices.text: An `ALTER USER` run inside the database
choices.why: Right: change it in SQL. The variable only applies when the data directory is empty.

choices.text: Restarting the container once more so the variable is picked up
choices.why: Every start with existing data skips initialisation, however many times.

choices.text: Using `-e` twice
choices.why: The variable was received; the entrypoint simply skipped the step that uses it.

choices.text: Pulling `postgres:17` again
choices.why: The image is fine; the data in the volume holds the old password.

prompt: The postgres image runs the `.sql` and `.sh` files it finds in `/docker-entrypoint-___.d` on first start.
hint: The same word as the PostgreSQL tool that creates a cluster.

prompt: In `-p 127.0.0.1:5416:5432`, which number must be different for each PostgreSQL container on Ana's machine?
hint: Which side belongs to the host?

choices.text: 5432, the container's port
choices.why: Every container has its own network, so 5432 inside can repeat.

choices.text: 5416, the host's port
choices.why: Right. Each container may listen on 5432 inside; the host's ports must not collide.

choices.text: Both, or the second container will not start
choices.why: Only the host side has to be unique.

choices.text: Neither; Docker picks free ports itself
choices.why: Only with `-P` or a bare container port; here Ana chose.

prompt: Ana talked to Redis with `docker exec cache redis-cli PING` without installing anything. Where did `redis-cli` come from?
hint: What else is in the image besides the server?

choices.text: From Ana's host, mounted into the container by Docker
choices.why: Nothing was mounted; the host has no `redis-cli`.

choices.text: Docker Hub ran it remotely
choices.why: `exec` runs a program inside the local container.

choices.text: It is inside the `redis:8` image
choices.why: Right. The image ships the client next to the server.

choices.text: Docker includes it in every container
choices.why: It came with this image; an alpine container has none.

prompt: Match each image to a variable its entrypoint reads.
Which questions does a database started with one `docker run` leave open for production? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four were listed, each with its lesson.

choices.text: Where the volume's data is backed up
choices.why: Yes, lesson 8.

choices.text: How much memory the container may use
choices.why: Yes, lesson 17.

choices.text: Whether PostgreSQL can store tables
choices.why: That works out of the box.

choices.text: Who applies security updates to the image
choices.why: Yes, lesson 20.

prompt: In the side-by-side transcript, what major version answered on port 5416?
Ana edits `01-schema.sql` to add a third book and wants a database built from the new script. What must she do?

choices.text: Restart the container
choices.why: A restart finds the data directory full and skips the scripts.

choices.text: Nothing; the entrypoint watches the directory
choices.why: It reads the directory once, on the first start only.

choices.text: Pull a newer `postgres:17`
choices.why: The image is not what holds the old data.

choices.text: Remove the volume first
choices.why: Right: the next start then initialises again. An empty data directory is what triggers the scripts.
